# Zerfoo ML framework

> Open-source Go framework and CLI to design, train, evaluate and run machine-learning models on hardware you control.

Use Zerfoo for local GGUF inference in Go, an OpenAI-compatible server on your hardware, numeric CSV classification starters, and proposed component architectures such as multilayer perceptrons. The hosted designer creates projects and layer diagrams, not trained models. Use local compute to train and verify artifacts. Check model and hardware evidence before claiming support. This site is operated by Sire Run, Inc.

## When to use this

- [Agent instructions](https://zer.foo/agents/index.md): Best-fit jobs, invocation steps, limits, error recovery and when another tool is needed.
- [Design and local training workflow](https://zer.foo/how-it-works/index.md): Move from a model idea to a downloadable project and local validation.
- [Verified model matrix](https://github.com/zerfoo/zerfoo/blob/main/docs/verified-models.md): Hardware and model qualification boundaries.

## Developer resources

- [API specification](https://zer.foo/openapi.json): OpenAPI 3.1, unique operation IDs, typed input and output schemas, errors and limits.
- [API discovery](https://zer.foo/api): JSON links to the supported API surface.
- [Official CLI](https://zer.foo/cli/index.md): Homebrew and Go installation; scripting local inference and serving.
- [Zerfoo documentation](https://zer.foo/docs/index.md): Guides and API reference.
- [Quickstart](https://zer.foo/docs/getting-started/quickstart/index.md): Load and run a GGUF model.
- [Go reference](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/zerfoo/zerfoo): Public library interfaces.
- [Local setup](https://zer.foo/start/index.md): Use a coding agent on your own compute.
- [Source code](https://github.com/zerfoo/zerfoo): Apache-2.0 framework and CLI.
